attacks.targetClaim: Insight 1: 'The training objective is settled... time conditioning is provably unnecessary... 4+ distinct groups converged independently... do NOT implement score entropy (SEDD has open NaN issues)'
attacks.attack: 'Provably unnecessary' is scoped-true, presented as universal: the RADD/Zheng factorization holds only for absorbing-state diffusion, and the report's own Insight 8 recommends budgeting a uniform/hybrid-noise arm (GIDD/UDLM) where time conditioning IS required and the simple masked-CE recipe no longer applies — 'settled' silently forecloses a fork the report elsewhere keeps open. The '4+ distinct groups' are not independent: RADD and LLaDA are the same lab (ML-GSAI), MDLM shares Cornell/Kuleshov lineage with the SEDD ecosystem, and the results cross-cite; this is convergence within one citation network, not independent replication (though the underlying algebra is genuinely correct, which caps severity). The anti-SEDD justification is issue-tracker cherry-picking: every research repo has open issues — the report itself cites MDLM's open issues when convenient (Windows friction) without downgrading MDLM — and SEDD's instability reports mostly concern uniform-state score entropy, while absorbing-state SEDD is mathematically the same objective being endorsed. Right advice, rhetorical evidence.

attacks.targetClaim: Insight 2: 'The architecture delta from a standard AR transformer is tiny... no GQA — pointless without KV cache... exactly 5 changes to a nanoGPT-style codebase'
attacks.attack: 'GQA is pointless without KV cache' is contradicted twice from within the corpus: Dream 7B (Qwen2.5-initialized) ships GQA and is a top-tier dLLM, and Insight 18 recommends block/semi-AR decoding 'from the start' — which restores KV caching (BD3-LM's selling point; Fast-dLLM even retrofits approximate caching onto vanilla dLLMs), making cache-friendly attention relevant again. The two insights cannot both stand as written. More broadly, '5 changes' counts diff lines, not engineering risk: the report's own Insight 14 documents materially higher gradient variance and LR fragility unique to the diffusion objective, Insight 5 documents both known laptop from-scratch attempts failing, and the sampler is an entire new subsystem with no AR analogue. The code delta is tiny; the behavioral delta is the project's main risk, and this framing invites underestimating it.

attacks.targetClaim: Insight 3: 'cheapest validated route... replicated independently by at least four parties... publicly endorsed by Karpathy... treat encoder-fine-tune as the guaranteed-working fallback'
attacks.attack: The 'four independent parties' are one social cascade: the same recipe, implemented within weeks of the same blog post and the same Karpathy signal-boost — that is one replication meme, not four independent validations, and 'endorsed by Karpathy' is authority, not evidence. Worse, all four demonstrate fluent-ish text continuation; none demonstrates arithmetic, which is this project's stated success criterion. BERT/RoBERTa WordPiece/BPE tokenizers chunk multi-digit numbers inconsistently and their pretraining corpora are math-poor, so the 'guaranteed-working fallback' is guaranteed at the wrong objective and may fail exactly where the build needs it (a char-level or digit-atomic from-scratch model could plausibly beat the fallback on arithmetic). Also internally inconsistent with Insight 15's real-time envelope: nathan-barry's 30 minutes was on an H200 (not laptop hardware), and RoBERTa-base at 125M sits at the edge of the '<150M fine-tuned' animation budget. Soften to: validated demo path for generic text, unvalidated for the math demo.

attacks.targetClaim: Insight 4: 'Complete small-scale reference implementations exist and agree on the recipe... MDLM's config supplies proven defaults (AdamW 3e-4, EMA 0.9999...)'
attacks.attack: They do not agree — the union of configs is presented as a consensus: LLaDA's linear p_mask=(1-eps)t+eps, MDLM's loglinear schedule + SUBS + antithetic sampling, and tiny-diffusion's char-level ad-hoc loop imply different effective loss weightings and schedules, and no source measures which matters at 10M scale; picking any one is a bet the report disguises as a settled recipe. 'Proven defaults' were proven at 110M+ params, large batch, OpenWebText — and one default is a concrete trap at laptop scale: EMA 0.9999 has a ~10,000-step time constant, so on a few-thousand-step laptop run the EMA weights are still dominated by initialization; evaluating the EMA model (as MDLM does) would silently evaluate a near-untrained network. nanoLLaDA is additionally a low-visibility hobby repo elevated to 'reference implementation' alongside peer-reviewed codebases — source-quality inflation. The flash-attn/Windows warning is fine but cites a 2023-era issue; the general point (strip CUDA-extension deps) survives, the specifics are stale.

attacks.targetClaim: Insight 5: 'The laptop feasibility envelope is 1-50M parameters on a narrow domain... plan for hours-to-days of training, absorbing-state (not raw D3PM)'
attacks.attack: The 'envelope' is built entirely from AR evidence (TinyStories models are AR; nanoGPT is AR; Chinchilla is AR-optimal single-epoch arithmetic) and is never multiplied by the report's own diffusion training tax: Insight 16 says to budget ~an order of magnitude extra wall-clock, which — applied honestly — shrinks the diffusion-adjusted envelope to a few million params or pushes 30-50M runs to multi-day/week territory, in direct tension with '1-50M feasible.' The only direct evidence is 0-for-2: and critically, one of the two failures (boesch.dev) ALREADY used the recommended fix — absorbing-state masked diffusion, ~2 hours on-device — so the proposed remedy is the thing that already failed, merely extrapolated to run longer. 'Hours-to-days' has zero successful instances behind it; the honest planning statement is 'no laptop-trained from-scratch diffusion LM of any quality exists in the record; the failure boundary is unknown and could exceed laptop patience entirely.' Calling a zero-success extrapolation an 'envelope' converts hypothesis into planning fact — the single most consequential overstatement in the report, since the flagship deliverable lives inside it. The insight's medium confidence and milestone framing are correct instincts that the 'envelope' vocabulary then undoes.

attacks.targetClaim: Insight 6: 'Math is the single worst case for diffusion's headline speed advantage, by converging theory, benchmark, and hardware evidence... CPU GGUF runs math prompts at 0.6x llama.cpp AR speed (15-16 steps needed)'
attacks.attack: The conclusion (don't sell speed) is right, but the 'converging evidence' is three weak legs stacked: (1) Feng et al. is a worst-case theoretical bound on a model class, not a measurement of trained models — it constrains guarantees, not observed behavior; (2) the 76.95→62.31 GSM8K collapse is one model (LLaDA-8B) under naive FIXED 2-token parallelism, while the very paper cited for 'dependency-guided decoding tests' (2604.02560, DEMASK — verified) headline-claims 1.7-2.2x speedup at matched-or-IMPROVED accuracy, i.e., the citation's own result is a rebuttal of the collapse framing it decorates; (3) the 0.6x CPU figure is a single community GGUF model card benchmarking ONE prompt per task — and I verified the card: the arithmetic prompt ('15 x 23?') converged in 4 steps, not 15-16 (16 was the Python is_prime prompt) — a factual error in a report that elsewhere mandates annotating every number with its eval config. Finally, scale mismatch: all speed evidence is 7-8B; at the build's 10-50M scale, even steps=length is tens of milliseconds on a laptop, so the entire speed question is close to moot for this project — which strengthens 'sell the mechanism' but means the dramatic 'single worst case' framing borrows big-model pain for a small-model decision.

attacks.targetClaim: Insight 7: 'Vanilla absorbing-state sampling has NO self-correction... confirmed at every scale... six different self-correction methods all failed at 288M'
attacks.attack: The mathematical core (committed tokens frozen) is true; 'confirmed at every scale' launders anecdotes into confirmation. I verified the HN source (item 48792131): it is real, but hr-diffuse-1-nano is a bidirectional Mamba-2 hybrid, cross-architecture distilled from SmolLM-135M for ~$500 — an exotic architecture and training route. Six failed methods on one distilled Mamba run by one builder establishes nothing general about from-scratch small transformers; 'small models don't doubt; they rationalize' is a quotable aphorism, not a scaling law. The Reddit Dream observation is user impression, not measurement. ReMDM 'stating it formally' is the vendor of the remasking cure formally diagnosing the disease it monetizes — mild conflict of interest. And there is an internal inconsistency the build will trip over: Insight 13 lists 'low-confidence remasking' as part of LLaDA's stock reference sampler while this insight says self-correction 'must be explicitly engineered' — the report never resolves that LLaDA-style remasking defers commitment within a step but never revises committed tokens, and stating both without the distinction will confuse the implementation and the UI honesty requirement.

attacks.targetClaim: Insight 8: 'A math DLLM with a small arithmetic vocabulary is precisely the small-vocab regime [where uniform noise competes]... budget an experiment arm for uniform/hybrid noise'
attacks.attack: Category error at the core: UDLM's small-vocab wins are on domains that are wholly small-vocabulary with short sequences and no compositional carry structure (molecules, DNA); a math LM still needs templated natural-language problem statements, and arithmetic's difficulty is carry/dependency structure, not vocabulary size — no source anywhere shows uniform or hybrid noise helping arithmetic specifically. GIDD's self-correction unlock was demonstrated compute-matched at ~100M+ on OpenWebText, not at 10M on math. The recommendation to fund an extra experimental arm directly contradicts the report's own compute pessimism (Insights 5 and 16: laptop compute is the binding constraint and the mainline may itself fail) — on a compute-starved project, a speculative-analogy arm is the first thing to cut, and the promised UI payoff (visible edits) is speculative squared: hybrid noise must both train well AND produce legible edits. Downgrade from 'budget an arm' to 'stretch goal if the mainline lands early.'

attacks.targetClaim: Insight 9: 'The strongest scientific argument FOR diffusion in this build — data-constrained multi-epoch advantage... is real but disputed in attribution'
attacks.attack: Two attacks, either fatal to the framing. (a) The concession swallows the claim: the report admits AR wins below a critical compute threshold 'a laptop may never cross.' If the build sits below the crossover — which Insights 5 and 16 jointly imply it does — then this literature predicts AR ≥ diffusion for THIS project, and labeling it 'the strongest argument FOR diffusion' is motivated framing of an argument that, at the relevant scale, points the other way. (b) The regime is self-imposed: the corpus is procedurally generated synthetic math (Insight 17), so data is unlimited by construction — the build can always sample fresh problems instead of re-epoching a frozen set. The 'data-constrained advantage' exists only if the experimenters artificially freeze the corpus, i.e., the experimental design manufactures the one regime where diffusion is claimed to win. The mandated regularized-AR control is necessary but insufficient: the natural strong baseline is AR trained on FRESH-SAMPLED data from the same generator, and against that baseline the entire argument dissolves. Reframe as: 'a datacenter-regime phenomenon, of unknown sign at laptop compute, testable here only under an artificial data freeze — include a fresh-data AR arm or drop the claim.'

attacks.targetClaim: Insight 10: 'Small diffusion models genuinely beat same-size AR on templated constraint/search math... MGDM at 85M hits 91.5% Countdown / 100% Sudoku... DoT-scratch hits 100% on 4x4/5x5 multiplication at 27x GPT-2-CoT throughput... scope the demo to templated symbolic tasks where the mechanism-level advantage is demonstrated at laptop-trainable sizes'
attacks.attack: The load-bearing phrase 'demonstrated at laptop-trainable sizes' is false as stated: MGDM is 85M — ABOVE the report's own 50M from-scratch envelope — trained on ~500k in-task problems on datacenter GPUs; DoT-scratch is GPT-2-scale with Plaid-lineage training compute. Nothing in the corpus demonstrates these capabilities at laptop training budgets, and Insight 5 explicitly admits no laptop-trained diffusion model with nontrivial math accuracy exists anywhere. 'Laptop-trainable sizes' conflates parameter count with training cost — the sleight of hand at the heart of the project pitch. Further: Countdown/Sudoku are the canonical diffusion-showcase tasks selected by the papers proposing the methods (task-selection bias); same-size AR models with scratchpad/reversed-digit formatting also reach ~100% on multi-digit multiplication, so the multiplication result demonstrates output formatting, not a diffusion mechanism advantage; and the '27x throughput' is an apples-to-oranges speed claim — diffusion emitting a short answer vs AR emitting a long CoT — i.e., fewer tokens written, not faster decoding, and it should not survive as a speed datapoint. Finally, the report never applies its own Insight 11 lens (GSM-Symbolic: templated small-model scores collapse under trivial perturbation) to these templated numbers — the centerpiece capability figures are exactly the genre of number the report's eval-hygiene section says to distrust.

attacks.targetClaim: Insight 11: 'Every dLLM math benchmark number in the corpus is an upper bound... GSM1K contamination checks show diffusion-family chat models dropping 2-7%... use float64 Gumbel sampling'
attacks.attack: The eval-hygiene insight fails its own hygiene test: I fetched arXiv 2601.22954 and it is 'Residual Context Diffusion Language Models' — an inference-recycling method paper, not a GSM1K contamination study. The 2-7% contamination figure is cited to the wrong paper and is currently unverifiable; it must be re-sourced or cut, and its presence inside the insight that lectures about wrong numbers (MMaDA POPE mix-up) is exactly the citation rot it warns against — which ironically strengthens the thesis while invalidating the specific claim. Additionally, the float64-Gumbel prescription is transplanted out of context: the float32 artifact corrupted GENERATIVE-PERPLEXITY comparisons (sampling entropy); it is irrelevant to exact-match arithmetic scoring, and Insight 13 already recommends temperature-0 for math, under which Gumbel noise isn't used at all. Prescribing it as build hygiene is harmless cargo-culting that signals rigor without adding any.

attacks.targetClaim: Insight 12: 'The real-time denoising UI is a solved, small problem... expect mostly near-left-to-right commit patterns on math — the visualization's any-order drama will be modest'
attacks.attack: The report understates its own citation into a project-killer it never names. I verified arXiv 2601.15165: it is 'The Flexibility Trap: Rethinking the Value of Arbitrary Order in Diffusion Language Models,' and it does not merely observe left-to-right tendencies — it argues arbitrary order ACTIVELY HARMS reasoning (models exploit flexibility to dodge high-uncertainty tokens) and achieves its best GSM8K result (89.1%) by constraining decoding to left-to-right. Now compose the report's own findings: optimal math decoding ≈ left-to-right (Insight 12's source), committed tokens never visibly change (Insight 7), semi-AR small blocks recommended (Insight 18), temperature-0 (Insight 13). The jointly-optimal configuration renders the centerpiece demo visually indistinguishable from a slow AR token streamer — the 'watch the model think in parallel' premise is negated by the very configuration the report recommends for accuracy. The UI is 'solved' as a rendering exercise, but the report never confronts that on the chosen domain there may be nothing distinctive to render, and the honest alternatives (deliberately suboptimal any-order decoding for show, or infilling/constraint demos where bidirectionality genuinely differs from AR) are never costed. The demo rationale needs redesign, not just softening: infilling — where the HN builder measured 14% recovery vs ~0 for AR — is the mechanism showcase the evidence actually supports.

attacks.targetClaim: Insight 13: 'The sampler design space is fully mapped and portable to a tiny model'
attacks.attack: 'Fully mapped' is false on its face — samplers are the most actively churning dLLM subfield (the report itself cites 2025-2026 papers still redrawing the map) — and 'portable to a tiny model' is asserted against the evidence: every named component was validated at 7-8B on AR-initialized models. The canonical loop's core assumption — usable confidence calibration — is precisely what the report's own sources deny at small scale ('small models don't doubt; they rationalize'; a 300k external critic beat the model's own confidence at error detection). If tiny-model confidences are miscalibrated, confidence-ordered unmasking can underperform random order, MaskGIT's cosine schedule (tuned on VQ image tokens) may be wrong for char-level math, and Fast-dLLM's threshold theorem guarantees nothing when the underlying marginals are bad. No tiny-scale sampler ablation exists anywhere in the corpus. Soften to: 'well charted at 7-8B; at build scale the sampler is an open experimental question — plan an ablation (random vs confidence vs margin vs entropy ordering), not an import.'

attacks.targetClaim: Insight 14: 'Training stability is a known, named risk with known fixes... A laptop build should adopt EMA + antithetic sampling + eps floor from day one'
attacks.attack: 'Known fixes' are known at 8B/1.2T-token scale and grafted downward without adjustment: LLaDA's LR crash at 1.2T tokens is irrelevant to a 200M-token run; P-POTS/MIRROR's GSM8K SFT gains are LLaDA-8B numbers with zero bearing on a 10-50M model; the variance-decomposition paper (2511.18159) is single, recent, unreplicated. The day-one prescription contains a live trap: EMA decay 0.9999 implies a ~10k-step averaging horizon, so on a few-thousand-step laptop run the EMA checkpoint is mostly initialization noise — adopting it 'from day one' can silently make every evaluation measure a near-untrained model, a failure mode far more likely to burn this build than the 1.2T-token loss spike the fix was invented for. The cheap items (eps floor, antithetic sampling) are fine; the recommendation should say 'rescale EMA decay to run length (~0.99-0.999) or skip it,' and should stop citing 8B SFT variance numbers as if they de-risk a tiny from-scratch run. Also note: whether 10M models even exhibit the named instability is unknown — the risk register may be borrowed along with the fixes.

attacks.targetClaim: Insight 15: 'Running or adapting existing 8B open dLLMs locally is a dead end... This forces the correct architecture decision'
attacks.attack: 'Dead end' rests on issue-tracker survivorship (only people with failures file issues; successful users are invisible) and config-specific failures: the LLaDA 24GB OOM report is full-finetune-shaped — LoRA/QLoRA-class adaptation of 8B models on 24GB is routine in the AR world and largely transfers; the '~31 hours for GSM8K' figure is a full-1319-problem benchmark artifact, irrelevant to a demo needing a dozen prompts; and the report's own verified source (diffuse-cpp GGUF card) shows 8B CPU inference at 27.7 tok/s on easy prompts — a 30-60s math completion is slow but perfectly demoable as a side-by-side exhibit ('here is a real one, slowly; here is ours, live'). The conclusion (train tiny for the real-time animation) is right and doesn't need the absolutism; 'forces' forecloses a cheap hybrid that would substantially strengthen the demo narrative. Soften 'dead end' to 'dead end for training and serious evaluation; viable as a canned or slow-side-exhibit inference demo.'

attacks.targetClaim: Insight 16: 'A diffusion training tax over AR is directionally certain but its magnitude is single-sourced... assume roughly an order of magnitude more wall-clock... partially reclaimable via the many-epoch small-corpus regime and modern efficiency tricks (Muon, etc.)'
attacks.attack: This insight and Insights 5 and 9 form an unreconciled triangle that the report never closes, and the project's go/no-go arithmetic lives inside the gap. Take the ~10x tax seriously and Insight 5's '1-50M laptop envelope' (built on untaxed AR datapoints) collapses; reclaim the tax via Insight 9's multi-epoch advantage and you must also import that literature's concession that AR wins below the compute crossover — which un-reclaims it. 'Partially reclaimable' carries no number, so the report's effective compute budget is undefined by its own sources: the honest range spans 'feasible weekend run' to 'weeks of laptop time,' and no insight commits. The 16x figure itself was measured for general-text likelihood parity at one scale in one unreplicated paper, and likelihood parity is the wrong target anyway — the build needs task accuracy on templated math, for which the tax is unmeasured in either direction. Finally 'Muon etc. transfer to single consumer GPUs' quietly extends AR-nanoGPT speedrun evidence to a bidirectional masked objective where Muon is untested. Demand: one reconciled budget table (params × tokens × tax × reclaim, with error bars) or delete the envelope numbers from Insight 5; as written, the two insights let a reader justify any conclusion.

attacks.targetClaim: Insight 17: 'Synthetic templated data is the highest-leverage axis... TinyGSM's 12.3M synthetic problems lift a 125M model to 63.1% GSM8K... grokking shows <1M params suffice for modular arithmetic'
attacks.attack: The two flagship citations are ornamental. TinyGSM is quadruply disanalogous: AR model, solutions expressed as Python EXECUTED BY AN INTERPRETER (the interpreter does the arithmetic — the model never computes), a 1.3B verifier for the headline figure, and a 12.3M-problem corpus (hundreds of millions of tokens) beyond any laptop pretraining budget — the report flags the interpreter caveat, then keeps the number anyway as halo. Grokking is single-task AR/MLP evidence that the report cites as support in the same breath as warning it is a hyperparameter lottery with unbounded wall-clock — having it both ways. The recipe's core instruction ('re-epoch heavily' on a fixed corpus) is the self-imposed data freeze attacked under Insight 9: with a generator in hand, fresh sampling is strictly available and is the stronger AR baseline, so the 'highest-leverage axis' as specified smuggles the diffusion-favoring design into the data plan. The sound residue — templated generation, fixed answer formats, external checker — needs none of these citations and should stand alone.

attacks.targetClaim: Insight 18: 'the build should support block mode from the start or use fixed short per-task canvases'
attacks.attack: The first half of the disjunction is scope creep against the report's own risk posture: BD3-LM adds per-block noise schedules, blockwise training logic, and new failure modes to a build whose primary documented risk (Insight 5) is achieving ANY coherent output; and the report's own chosen scope (Insight 10: fixed-format templated tasks) makes fixed short canvases trivially sufficient — block mode solves variable length and KV caching, problems the scope already eliminated. Citation drift compounds it: verified, 2602.07546 is LR-DLLM, an inference-time length-regularization paper — it supports the 'fixed length is a handicap' clause but actually demonstrates an inference-only mitigation, further undercutting 'must support block mode from the start.' And the stacking problem: blocks + left-to-right confidence tendency + frozen commits + temperature-0 reconstructs an AR-like decoder (see the Insight 12 attack) — each mitigation individually reasonable, jointly dissolving the differentiation the project exists to demonstrate. Keep the second disjunct ('fixed short per-task canvases'), demote block mode to a later milestone.

attacks.targetClaim: Portfolio-level: the report's overall synthesis that a laptop-trained 10-50M diffusion model doing visible-denoising math is a supported build target
attacks.attack: No single point in (params, training compute, task, UI) space is supported by all the evidence simultaneously — every defense is pairwise. Capability evidence (MGDM 91.5% Countdown, DoT multiplication) lives at 85M+/datacenter compute; feasibility evidence (tiny-diffusion, 20 A100-minutes) lives at 10M/char-level Shakespeare with no math; the two on-laptop datapoints are both failures; the UI's wow-factor evidence lives at 7-8B and, per the report's own cited 'Flexibility Trap' paper, disappears under math-optimal decoding settings. The flagship configuration — 10-50M params, laptop training budget, nontrivial arithmetic accuracy, dramatic any-order visualization — is an unsampled corner of the space defended by citations that each support a different corner. The report should state this compositional gap as its headline risk instead of distributing it across seventeen hedges: the most probable outcome per its own evidence is a model that trains slowly, does modest templated arithmetic at best, and decodes near-left-to-right with no visible self-correction. The defensible pivots the evidence DOES support — infilling demos (where diffusion's advantage over AR is real and measured at 288M: 14% vs ~0), side-by-side AR-vs-diffusion training curves as the pedagogical artifact, and deliberately non-optimal decoding for visualization — are present in fragments but never assembled into the recommendation.

biases: Motivated-reasoning / conclusion-first bias: the report is assembled to justify a predetermined build (laptop diffusion LM). Disconfirming evidence is included but quarantined — the 0-for-2 laptop failure record, the ~16x training tax, and the AR-wins-below-crossover concession each appear as hedges inside insights whose headlines still assert feasibility ('envelope', 'strongest argument FOR', 'validated route'). Evidence updates the footnotes, never the conclusions.

Scale-transfer bias (bidirectional): 7-8B results — samplers, stability fixes, parallelism collapse, SFT variance numbers, VRAM failures — are freely projected onto a 10-50M from-scratch build where none are validated; simultaneously, tiny-scale AR results (TinyStories, nanoGPT, Chinchilla) are projected onto diffusion without applying the report's own diffusion tax. Optimistic and pessimistic claims both borrow evidence from the wrong scale.

Vendor bias / self-graded homework: nearly every capability and fix claim originates from the method's own paper (MGDM, DoT, ReMDM, GIDD, UDLM, BD3-LM, Fast-dLLM, P-POTS/MIRROR, LLaDA GUIDELINES), with no third-party small-scale replication. ReMDM both formally diagnoses the no-self-correction disease and sells the remasking cure; Countdown/Sudoku are showcase tasks selected by the diffusion papers that win them.

Social-cascade double counting: the 'four independent' encoder-finetune replications are one Karpathy-amplified recipe re-implemented within weeks — one meme counted four times; 'publicly endorsed by Karpathy' is treated as evidence.

Issue-tracker asymmetry / survivorship inversion: open GitHub issues are used as disqualifying evidence against SEDD and against local 8B use, while open issues on endorsed repos (MDLM) are framed as mere porting friction; issue trackers structurally overrepresent failures since successful users file nothing.

AR-evidence laundering: the laptop feasibility envelope (Insight 5) is triangulated entirely from AR datapoints and then applied to diffusion; Chinchilla arithmetic is cited for a regime (multi-epoch, diffusion) where it does not apply.

Citation decoration and rot: at least one confirmed wrong-paper citation (arXiv 2601.22954, cited for GSM1K contamination, is actually 'Residual Context Diffusion Language Models'), one citation whose headline result contradicts the sentence it supports (DEMASK's 1.7-2.2x-speedup-at-matched-accuracy cited for parallelism fragility), one understated citation ('The Flexibility Trap' says any-order decoding actively hurts math, not merely 'trends left-to-right'), and one misread benchmark detail (the GGUF card's arithmetic prompt took 4 steps, not 15-16). In a corpus that already caught one number error (MMaDA), every post-2025 citation should be treated as unverified until fetched.

Task-framing bias in the demo rationale: 'math' is quietly narrowed to templated constraint/search tasks where diffusion showcases exist, while the UI narrative continues to trade on the general 'watch it think in parallel' story that the math-optimal configuration (left-to-right, frozen commits, temperature-0, small blocks) negates.
claimsToRemove: REMOVE: 'no GQA — pointless without KV cache' (Insight 2) — contradicted by Dream's GQA and by the report's own block-mode recommendation restoring KV caching.
REMOVE: '27x GPT-2-CoT throughput' as a speed datapoint (Insight 10) — it measures shorter outputs (no CoT tokens), not faster decoding; apples-to-oranges.

REMOVE or RE-SOURCE: the GSM1K contamination sentence's citation (Insight 11) — arXiv 2601.22954 is 'Residual Context Diffusion Language Models', not a contamination study; the 2-7% figure is currently unsourced.

REMOVE: TinyGSM 63.1%/81.5% figures from the data recipe rationale (Insight 17), or fence them explicitly as AR + Python-interpreter + 1.3B-verifier results with no quantitative bearing on a text-only tiny diffusion model.
SOFTEN: 'time conditioning is provably unnecessary' (Insight 1) → scope to absorbing-state masked diffusion; state it does not hold for the uniform/hybrid arm recommended in Insight 8.

SOFTEN: 'replicated independently by at least four parties' and 'guaranteed-working fallback' (Insight 3) → one social cascade of the same recipe; guaranteed only for fluent text, unvalidated for arithmetic; flag digit-tokenization risk.

SOFTEN: 'The laptop feasibility envelope is 1-50M parameters' (Insight 5) → present as an untested hypothesis extrapolated from AR evidence; state plainly that zero successful laptop from-scratch diffusion LMs exist and that one of the two failures already used the recommended absorbing-state recipe.
SOFTEN: 'plan for hours-to-days of training' (Insight 5) → 'lower bound unknown; both documented attempts failed at the minutes-to-hours scale; days-scale success is extrapolation, not observation.'
SOFTEN: '15-16 steps needed' for CPU math (Insight 6) → per the verified model card: 4 steps for the arithmetic prompt, 16 for the Python prompt; single-prompt community benchmark — annotate as such.

SOFTEN: 'the most parallelism-fragile benchmark in dependency-guided decoding tests' (Insight 6) → note the cited DEMASK paper's own headline is 1.7-2.2x speedup at matched-or-improved accuracy; fragility applies to naive fixed parallelism.

SOFTEN: 'use float64 Gumbel sampling' as build hygiene (Insight 11) → relevant only to generative-perplexity comparisons; moot under the temperature-0 math decoding the report itself recommends.
